title.narrative: Sustainable Rural Infrastructure and Watershed Management Sector Project

description.narrative: The project is intended to address issues of PRI and watershed management in mountainous provinces of Northern Lao PDR by using an integrated land use planning approach that integrates efficient, sustainable and climate resilient rural infrastructure, and feasible watershed protection measures. For an ecosystem based sustainable rural development, infrastructure and the watershed have to be considered simultaneously. The expected impact of the project will be to achieve sustainable and inclusive rural development. The outcome of the project will be to enhance sustainable, market oriented agricultural production and natural resources management in selected watersheds.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: High value agricultural production, natural resources management, status of women and community nutrition improved.

Land area of 223,000 ha rehabilitated. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: PLUP strategies and plans for Xieng Khouang and Houaphan are approved in 23 September and 11 October 2024. Catchment studies to guide provincial development plans have been completed. UXO clearance in Houaphan and Xieng Khouang were already awarded and under implementation. As of Q4 2025, around 745 ha of the 900 ha in Houphan have been surveyed and cleared, and around 960 ha of the 1,200 ha have been cleared in Xieng Khouang. Data Source: PPMS

In target areas, 60% of women of reproductive age meet minimum dietary diversity. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Village nutrition clubs have been formed in 10 pilot villages (all women), and DAFO staff trained to roll out the nutrition program by establishing district nutrition teams to eventually cover 200 villages. Surveys are planned to provide M&E data. At this stage progress has not been measured, but field observations and activities undertaken indicate progress is significantly higher than the baseline figure. Data Source: Social Surveys results

4,400 women producing HVC, and livestock will be established supported. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Surveys are underway to measure the number of women producing HVC and livestock. Data Source: Provincial and district reports on key commercial crop production and PPMS.

In modernized subproject areas: (i) average agriculture profitability increased to $1,060/ha (2018 baseline: $494/ha); and (ii) 50% increase in average household income levels from HVC and livestock production. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Four Batch 1 Subprojects were operational during the 2023-2024 dry season. HVC crop calendar developed with WUGs for four Batch 1 Subprojects. Extension work commenced in 2024 to help diversify into HVCs. No measurable progress of baseline at this stage. Data Source: Provincial and district reports on key commercial crop production and PPMS. Baseline value: $494; $5070

Output: Command area irrigation reliability improved Indicator: Implementation of 18 market plans - one for each subproject, with at least 45% of participants are women's participation in the market plan consultations and implementation. Output: Indicator Indicator: 2 WUAs, with 25% of management[g] consisting of females established (2018 baseline: 0) (OP 5.1) Progress/Status: The number of WUAs to be established is decreased from 18 to 2. This reflects the experience of SRIWMSP and other irrigation sector projects where the establishment of WUAs has proven to be unfeasible. DOI considers it is far more effective to support the two existing WUAs and strengthen WUGs due to lack of demand for new WUAs. Data Source: PPMS Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 28 subprojects modernized with: (i) dry season irrigated agriculture on 4,400 ha (2018 baseline: 2,242 ha); (ii) 4,400 ha of WSIA (2018 baseline 3,646 ha); and (iii) 100 km of year-round access and service roads. (2018 baseline: 30km). (OP 5.3) Progress/Status: In 4 RSP schemes modernized irrigation introduced, completed and handed over to the WUGs. These RSPs will enable incremental cropping on 275 ha in the wet season and 551 ha in the dry season, for an average cost of $4,697 per incremental ha serving 2,251 households.
Feasibility Studies and DEDs for 8 ASPs under Batch 2 are completed. These will allow incremental cropping on 600 ha in the wet season and 985 ha in the dry season, for an average cost of $3,144 per incremental ha, serving 3,139 households. Preparations for Batch 3 subprojects are ongoing with data collection for topographical, geotechnical, and hydrological surveys, preparation of draft FSRs, pre-designs and final draft OED, and preparation of draft IEEs and social guard assessments.
It has been agreed that some savings generated in other outputs will be reallocated to Output 3 to finance about 10 additional irrigation schemes (Batch 4) with command areas in the range 20-50 hectares each in Houaphan and Xieng Khouang. However, in October 2024, DOI requested to use this savings for emergency rehabilitation of irrigation schemes damaged by 2 typhoons. During the Review Mission in December 2024, ADB and DOI agreed on this new scope and selected 6 damaged irrigation schemes to be funded under the loan. As of June 2025, DED, bidding and evaluation for the five DRA subprojects are all complete, but contract award is waiting for approval of Ministry of Finance.
The contracts for the 4 DRA contracts were signed in September 2025. Data Source: PPMS Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 9 PLUPs implemented. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The Project and DOI agreed to proceed with one pilot land use change activity for demonstration purposes in each of the 9 subproject watershed areas in Houaphan and Xieng Khouang.
As of October 2024, the PLUPs for XiengKhuang and Houaphan has been approved by ADB with budget of $500,000 each province. Implementation of this PLUPs are ongoing.
As of June 2025, work plans and budgets for the two pilot land use change plans have been prepared for two catchments, one in Houaphan (eight villages) and another in Xieng Khouang (three villages), and implementation activities are now underway
As of Q4 2025, PLUPs are under implementation Data Source: PPMS

Output: Indicator Indicator: NNSPA program implemented Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: WFP was mobilized in Feb 2023. Ten initial pilot villages have been identified, and WFP has been active in the ten target villages with the establishment of District Nutrition Teams and with training in Linking Agriculture to Nutrition and Natural Resources (LANN) for pilot and on-going for scale up.
Addressing environmental factors within villages, particularly water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH), is crucial to achieving nutritional impact. WFP/SNV will identify WASH infrastructure needs in each village, prioritizing the 37 villages in irrigation subproject areas to generate synergies and integration. WFP engaged a service provider to assess WASH facilities and needs across the target villages and recommended prioritizing interventions across three levels within communities (households; health centers; schools). The report has been with DOI since December 2024 for consideration and agreement on the priority listing. The implementation of WASH activities in terms of selection, design and procurement have not yet commenced. Data Source: PPMS
